item.description: In 2017, Yvonne Thomson founded UKHarvest to address food waste and assist individuals facing food insecurity. Its initiatives, including Community Food Hubs and Grub Clubs, offer not only affordable food but also valuable education. item.title: Antipodes Island Sees Ground Beetle Numbers Surge 40-Fold After Mice Eradication
item.description: The successful removal of invasive house mice from Antipodes Island has spurred a remarkable resurgence in ground beetle populations, which have increased to around 40 times their former numbers. item.title: In 1987, an amateur fossil hunter found a T. rex in South Dakota; the $31.8 million skeleton now stands in Abu Dhabi
item.description: In 1987, Stan Sacrison found a T. rex skeleton in South Dakota, which was later sold for $31.8 million. Initially misidentified, the bones were correctly recognized as belonging to a T. rex in 1992. After years at the Black Hills Institute, the skeleton was auctioned and purchased for a museum in Abu Dhabi. Stan is now displayed in a dramatic scene depicting conflicts with another T. rex. item.title: In 1600, William Gilbert called Earth a giant magnet; his book sold for Rs 58.5 lakh in 2026
item.description: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.
